tweets.text:
All arbitrage can be condensed into a few lines. Because arbitrage is so "solved", under the no-free-lunch theorem, it cannot come easy.

You either have some execution alpha in being able to reduce slippage and inventory risks, have some structural alpha in being able to reduce your costs, have some prediction alpha in being able to approximate the effects of the execution/structural alpha; or just have great operational risk management in being able to survive the steamroller.

---
profit =
# theoretical profit from collapsing the spread
(price_A_start_observed
- price_B_start_observed)
- (price_A_end_fair
- price_B_end_fair)

# slippage
- (price_A_start_slippage
+ price_B_start_slippage)
- (price_A_end_slippage
+ price_B_end_slippage)

# inventory risks
- (target_inventory_A_pnl - actual_inventory_A_pnl)
- (target_inventory_B_pnl - actual_inventory_B_pnl)

# costs
- (price_A_start_cost
+ price_B_start_cost)
- (price_A_end_cost
+ price_B_end_cost)
- (price_A_inventory_cost
+ price_B_inventory_cost)

Assuming hedge ratio = 1; and the spread is rich.

tweets.text:
What does the average trader care about? After being heads down building @dragonswap_dex, for me it essentially comes down to these 2 things.

1. Execution = speed + cost efficiency + capital efficiency + trade efficiency (slippage, fill quality)
2. Security

Users will go where they get best mix of security and execution.

The other stuff like incentives, platform (desktop vs mobile), UX, GTM, partnerships etc are all things to consider, but realistically these things above are what traders really NEED. Everything else is secondary.

You won't use a random new DEX for $10 better quote. But between Uniswap and Sushiswap? You'll might pick whoever saves you $5.

Obviously there are some users that don't care about $5. They'll just use Uniswap because familiar, but that's because Uniswap was able to effectively demonstrate point 1 + 2 above the quickest. Now the "mental cost" to change is too high.

That's the approach we're undertaking with DragonSwap as well, by focusing on unparalleled execution, paired with security we can create the infrastructure that allows users to get a CEX grade experience with custody.

Closed test trước public luôn là lúc “lộ chất” thật của một sản phẩm vì đây là lúc bị test bởi trader thực, không phải user farm.

@Nasun_io đang làm khá đúng với Pado:

• Không mass onboarding vội  
• Cho test full flow (execution, slippage, fee)  
• Open feedback cả tốt lẫn xấu  

Với mình, một spot product đáng dùng không nằm ở UI hay incentive, mà ở mấy thứ này:

• Execution có ổn định không, có bị delay / trượt giá vô lý không  
• Fee có minh bạch hay có hidden cost  
• Liquidity đủ sâu để trade size hay chỉ hợp retail nhỏ  
• UX từ connect → trade → confirm có mượt không  

24h closed test kiểu này là đủ để simulate điều kiện thị trường thật, không phải kiểu test cho có.

Nếu @Nasun_io iterate tốt sau vòng này, Pado có thể sẽ là một trong những sản phẩm đáng chú ý khi public devnet mở.
